issues.body: ProofSummary says the store value is private and not disclosed to the verifier, while the prover publishes operand_enc. The only provable values are the four entries in the shipped OPERAND_ENC table (24, 25, 30, 42), making operand_enc a trivially enumerable identifier for the witness. The generic research-track/not-audited caveat does not make the panel's specific nondisclosure statement true. The E2E check only asserts that the numeric field 30 is absent; it does not test whether the public commitment identifies 30 by dictionary lookup.
issues.fix_hint: Remove or narrowly qualify the nondisclosure claim to state that the raw digits are private but the deterministic operand commitment may reveal low-entropy values by enumeration. Update the README and E2E description/assertions consistently. If actual value hiding is intended, use a hiding commitment with verifier-bound randomness and test the resulting disclosure model; do not claim it from absence of the literal integer alone.
issues.title: Public operand_enc reveals witnesses from the tiny shipped domain

verdict.summary: Round 4 regresses from the finding-free prior round: the ZK panel makes a concrete nondisclosure claim that its implementation and browser test do not establish. Although the raw integer is not a public input, operand_enc is a deterministic public encoding drawn from a shipped four-value table, so a verifier can enumerate the table and recover the selected value. The external-audit caveat does not cure the specific false claim that the value is hidden. The test is non-vacuous as an execution test, but its privacy assertion checks only that the integer field 30 is absent and misses this dictionary disclosure channel.
